A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The complete 24-page v2 and 26-page v3, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original simulations with random and clustered preferences and experiments using the Sushi dataset, with outcomes in Table 1 and Figures 1–3.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original simulation and Sushi-dataset results in Table 1 and Figures 1–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 adds deterministic sampling of every winner–other-arm pair before its randomized loop and removes the exploitation-stage estimate update. Algorithm 1 fixes accumulation of observations and replaces self-duel sampling with known diagonal probabilities of 1/2. These are localized procedural corrections within the retained algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate random preferences, majority/minority clustered preferences, and the same Sushi rankings with 10 items and 5 or 10 user clusters. No dataset, task, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Utilitarian-ETC, Utilitarian-ε-Greedy, and Uniform-Over-Users. Table 1 retains the same practice of reporting the best utilitarian comparator for each metric.

E3.justification: The reported experimental configurations, preprocessing, horizons, metrics, and exploration multipliers are retained. Section 5.2 corrects K=20 to K=10 for D=20, matching Figure 1(f) already present in v2. The added solver settings and metric explanations disclose existing experiments rather than establish a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds a brief validation statement confirming that every Sushi cluster has a unique Condorcet winner after boundary projection, with no further adjustments required. The existing clustered-preference robustness analysis remains unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 30 independent runs and 95% uncertainty intervals. V3 newly specifies that table ± values and shaded figure regions represent confidence intervals calculated as 1.96 times the standard error; it does not report additional runs.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Table 1 and plotted results in Figures 1–3 are unchanged. The limited addition is Section 5.4's qualitative finding that all processed Sushi clusters satisfy the unique-winner assumption without further adjustment.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1 substantially revise the lower-bound construction, winner assignments, single-user perturbation, KL argument, and regret inequalities. V3 explicitly assumes independent feedback, restricts Theorem 4.1 to even K and D, and adds positive-gap and confidence-parameter conditions. Appendices A.2–A.3 correct missing policy weights and scaled-score concentration factors and incorporate the new warm-up phase into the sampling and regret arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same fairness formulation, two algorithms, lower-bound order, and matching dependence on the time horizon. The conclusion's added min(K,D) factor repeats a claim already stated in v2's abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: V3 explains the unmatched dependence on K, D, and the preference gap, distinguishing winner-identification costs from fairness-related hardness. It discusses possible extensions to other welfare functions and their limitations, and clarifies the distinction between product-based regret and cumulative geometric-mean welfare.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents Frank–Wolfe initialization, step sizes, the 10^-12 numerical floor, a 300-iteration maximum, and the 2×10^-4 stopping threshold. It also clarifies the exploration-length multiplier and repairs duel-count bookkeeping and subroutine interfaces in Appendix B.

R1.justification: V3 adds Busa-Fekete et al. (2017) when discussing generalized Gini welfare and possible extensions. The main research positioning remains unchanged; the Nash and Hastie reference edits correct bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: V3 corrects terminology, notation references, and experimental-description inconsistencies; revises parts of the proof exposition; and adds focused explanatory paragraphs. Appendix headings become 'Proofs' and 'Condorcet-Winner Identification Algorithms,' while the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: The same three figures and two tables are retained. Figure 2 is reduced in size, Figure 3 and several algorithm/table blocks move, and Table 2 accommodates revised mathematical conditions. Plot panels, axes, legends, and graphical results remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens the support for the paper's central regret guarantees: it revises the lower-bound construction, corrects policy-weight and scaled-score errors in the upper-bound arguments, and adds the initialization needed for the sampling bound. These address substantive mathematical and algorithmic deficiencies in v2. Clearer solver specifications, uncertainty reporting, and applicability limitations reinforce the improvement. The benchmark results remain unchanged, so the gain concerns correctness and transparency rather than demonstrated performance.
